summary: Re-verified toast v2 fix and supplier contact data fix. Supplier contact data fix is FULLY WORKING (S2560 SANTOSHI ENTERPRISES shows Contact Person='Yogesh Singh', Phone='+91 8750495001'). Toast fix v2 is PARTIALLY fixed: text color now correctly renders green/red per type (confirmed via getComputedStyle on [data-title]: error=#B42318, success=#027A48), BUT the tinted background (light red/green) still does NOT apply - background stayed white (rgb(255,255,255)) for both success and error toasts. Root cause identified: the 'group' class and the 'group-data-[type=x]:!bg-[...]' utility classes are applied to the SAME <li data-sonner-toast> element (via the 'toast' classNames key). Tailwind's group-data-* variant generates a DESCENDANT selector (.group[data-type=x] &), which requires 'group' to be on an ANCESTOR of the styled element, not the same element. Since title/description are nested children of the <li>, their group-data-[type=x]:!text-[...] classes correctly match (li is ancestor) - that's why text color works. But the <li>'s own bg/border group-data-[type=x] classes never match themselves. This is a real, reproducible bug distinct from the v1 issue.

ui_bugs.issue: Toast background/border color-coding still not applied. Confirmed via getComputedStyle: li background stays rgb(255,255,255) (white) for both error and success toasts instead of the intended #FEF3F2 (error) / #ECFDF3 (success). Text color DOES work correctly now (error title color=rgb(180,35,24)=#B42318, success title color=rgb(2,122,72)=#027A48) since title is a descendant of the <li> group element. RCA: group-data-[type=x]:!bg-[...] classes are applied to the 'toast' key which targets the <li> itself - the SAME element that carries the 'group' class - so the descendant selector '.group[data-type=x] &' generated by Tailwind never matches (group must be an ancestor, not self). Fix: move the type-specific bg/border classes to be applied conditionally via toast() call options or use `[data-type=x]&` self-referential attribute selector instead of group-data variant for the bg/border on the 'toast' key specifically.

critical_code_review_comments: group-data-[x] Tailwind variant only matches when 'group' class is on an ANCESTOR of the element carrying the utility class - it cannot be used to self-style the same element that has 'group'. This was the remaining bug after v2's otherwise-correct diagnosis of the v1 issue (competing !important classes) - the fix correctly resolved title/description descendant color-coding but missed that the toast/li's own bg-color needed the non-group 'data-[type=x]:' variant instead.

rca of the issue: Tailwind's `group-data-[attr=val]:` variant compiles to a descendant CSS selector of the form `.group[data-attr=val] &` (or similar with :where wrappers), meaning the element carrying data-attr=val AND class='group' must be an ANCESTOR of the element being styled - it cannot match utilities placed on that same element. In sonner.jsx, the 'toast' classNames key places both 'group' and 'group-data-[type=x]:!bg-[...]' on the identical <li data-sonner-toast data-type='x'> element, so the generated descendant selector never matches itself, leaving the base 'bg-white' (no !important, but nothing overrides it) as the only applicable background rule. In contrast, the 'title'/'description' classNames keys style a genuinely nested child <div> of that <li>, so the same group-data-[type=x] variant correctly resolves against the ancestor <li>, which is why text color now works but background does not.
